steps.note: PC bought-items shell. The doc-level 12s watchdog shows a soft error if we are slow — harmless: we boot the app ourselves before it matters, and the app renders over the placeholder. REQUIRES a logged-in buyer session passed via session_id (fresh flow sessions ride the default jar; see flow.md).

SSR shell marker. The React app itself never loads here — the shell carries no script tag for it; the tbnav loader is supposed to fetch-load it and that step does not fire in diting (engine gap, own issue).

Sniff fetch/XHR for queryboughtlistv2 bodies -> parse the app's main.js url out of window.pcMyTaobaoMenuList urlList (never hardcode the 0.x version) -> pushState('/') so the ice.js browser router matches route '/' (standalone basename 404s the full trade path) -> fetch + inject the bundle. The app then fires its own baxia-signed mtop — manual mtop.request from page context is silently swallowed, so letting the real app run is the only door.
App booted + first mtop body sniffed. A timeout here means login lost or punish — inspect the session verdict by hand.

Drive the Pagination fiber's onChange directly (synthetic .click() freezes at page 2). Target page comes from the DATA — pageControl.nextPageIndex of the last sniffed body — never the DOM (antd's active item lags arbitrarily this way, seen showing 1 on page 4) and never a counter. 'grew' is data-aware (new orderIds AND hasMore!==false) because the app refetches the same page on back-to-back calls (that runaway burned a whole step budget); a 1.5s settle plus one in-script retry at target+1 absorbs a stray dup. Bare-object return — a JSON.stringify'd save is a string and branch dotted-paths die on it.
Loop while pages keep coming; falls through on the first dry page (hasMore exhausted). max_steps=800 bounds a runaway (data-aware 'grew' already stops a dup-page loop; 800 ≈ 397 pages ceiling).
Parse every sniffed JSONP body, fold shopInfo_*/orderItemInfo_* islands into one order per orderId, newest first. Receipt carries the full history.
